description: This plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and "ACC (%)" for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale for values above zero, displaying tick marks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from approximately 35 to 68, with tick marks at intervals of 5 from 45 to 65. All methods are represented by solid lines and exhibit an upward trend across four data points located at approximate x-values of 3, 30, 300, and 3000. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at an ACC of approximately 38, rising to 41.5 and 43.5, and ending at 44. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning at roughly 39.5, increasing to 43 and 46, and finishing at 47.5. The "IKE" method uses a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting at about 43, rising to 45 and 46.5, and ending at 49.5. The "MEND" method is depicted by a brown line with diamond markers, starting at 44.5, increasing to 48.5 and 54, and concluding at 56.5. The "MEMIT" method is represented by a purple line with hexagon markers, beginning at 43.5, rising to 51 and 53, and ending at 54.5. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a green line with square markers, starting at the highest initial value of 51, increasing to 57 and 62.5, and reaching a peak of approximately 66 at the final data point.
